working_title: Scotland's Open Coast Without the Open Price Tag: A Practical Guide to Playing the Ayrshire Gailes Circuit
angle: Ayrshire has three Open Championship venues that get all the attention and the eye-watering green fees to match — but sandwiched between them is a cluster of championship-calibre links (Western Gailes, Glasgow Gailes, Dundonald Links, Kilmarnock Barassie, West Kilbride, and Prestwick St Nicholas) that most visiting golfers walk straight past. The post makes the case for building a trip around this 'second tier' rather than — or as relief rounds alongside — the marquee names, with honest notes on visitor access, what each course actually plays like, and how to string them into a practical itinerary from a Troon base.
research_notes:
- Ayrshire coast contains three Open Championship venues: Royal Troon, Prestwick (birthplace of the Open in 1860), and Turnberry (Ailsa course). These anchor most visitors' itineraries.
- Within 20 minutes of each other: Western Gailes, Dundonald Links, Glasgow Gailes (Gailes Links), Kilmarnock (Barassie), West Kilbride, Irvine Golf Club, Prestwick St Nicholas.
- Troon is considered the practical base: Royal Troon is in the town, Prestwick and Western Gailes are ten minutes either side, Turnberry 40 minutes south.
- Western Gailes: founded 1897, narrow strip of dune land between the Firth of Clyde and the Ayrshire Coast Line railway. Frequently used as Open Qualifying course. 2026 published green fees range from £95 (winter weekday) to £335 (summer Saturday). Includes soup and sandwiches on weekday rounds (peak season). Handicap certificate required. Visitor-friendly reputation.
- Glasgow Golf Club (Gailes Links): links course of Glasgow Golf Club (founded 1787), opened at Gailes in 1892, designed by Willie Park Jnr, par 71, 6,903 yards. 2026 green fees £95 (winter) to £180 (summer), checked June 2026. Visitor days restricted — contact club directly. Handicap certificate required.
- Dundonald Links: modern resort links, has hosted Scottish Open. 2026 green fees from around £95–£195 per round (per Birdiebrae). Bookable online.
- Kilmarnock (Barassie): 27 holes of proper links just outside Troon. Part of Ayrshire Golf Pass alongside Irvine Golf Club, Prestwick St Nicholas, and West Kilbride.
- West Kilbride Golf Club: 6,523 yards from championship tees, panoramic views across Firth of Clyde to Arran. 2026 published green fees: April/October £95–£125 (round/day, 1–3 players), May–September £125–£165. Has hosted R&A Seniors Home Internationals, Scottish Boys' Championship, Scottish PGA Championship. Visitors by prior arrangement, weekdays and after 3pm weekends.
- Prestwick St Nicholas: sits opposite championship Prestwick, same Old Tom Morris-era pedigree. Noted as a budget-friendly option (~£90–£130 per round).
- Irvine Golf Club (Bogside): listed as approximately £90 per round.
- Ayrshire Golf Pass: Kilmarnock Barassie, Irvine Golf Club, Prestwick St Nicholas, and West Kilbride combined pass — value multi-course option.
- Gailes Golf Experience (separate package): Dundonald Links, Gailes Links, and Western Gailes; 2026 pricing £215 (March) up to from £430 (May–September) per person for all three rounds.
- Ayrshire Links Experience: Dundonald Links, Barassie Links, Irvine Golf Club; 2026 pricing £215 (March) to from £430 (May–September) per person for three rounds.
- Western Gailes is railway-accessible from Glasgow (Ayrshire Coast Line runs alongside the course) — practical for a day trip.
- Royal Troon visitor access: limited weekday slots only, months of advance booking needed.
- Troon municipal Darley course: council-run links, reportedly £20–£28 — useful for a warm-up or budget day.
- Do NOT fabricate specific yardages, par figures, or green fees for any course not listed above — describe in general terms.
- Solway Links near Southerness (Dumfries and Galloway) closed in 2020 — do not include.
must_avoid:
- No fabricated green fees, yardages, or specs for courses where figures were not found in research — describe in general terms only.
- Dumfries and Galloway is already covered in a published post (scotland-s-forgotten-golf-corner-a-practical-guide-to-playing-dumfries-and-galloway-2026-08-20) — do not overlap into that region.
- Scotland's Kintyre (Machrihanish) is covered in another published post — do not stray into Kintyre/Islay territory.
- East Lothian and Angus are also covered — keep the post firmly on the Ayrshire coast.
- No gambling/betting content.
- No invented quotes attributed to reviewers, pros, or club officials.
- No personal anecdotes implying the site owner has played these courses unless the brief is explicitly updated with that information.
- No health or injury advice beyond generic.
- No financial advice on affordability — describe costs factually, not as a recommendation on whether they represent value for a reader's personal budget.
- Affiliate links only for approved partners; any in-content affiliate link requires a one-line disclosure near the top of the post.
- UK English throughout (favour, colour, -ise endings, etc.).
- No em dashes anywhere in the post.
